parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Fig. 7.1 shows a coil at rest in a uniform magnetic field that is parallel to the axis of the coil.

[[fig:f1]]

The coil is connected to a centre-zero voltmeter.

The flux density *B* of the uniform magnetic field varies with time *t* as shown in Fig. 7.2.

[[fig:f2]]

The coil consists of 340 turns, each of cross-sectional area 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ m².
parts.text: Calculate the maximum magnetic flux through one turn of the coil.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the maximum rate of change of magnetic flux linkage in the coil.

answer.symbol: maximum rate of change of flux linkage

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State the maximum electromotive force (e.m.f.) *V*₀ induced across the coil.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
On Fig. 7.3, sketch the variation of the e.m.f. *V* induced across the coil with *t* from *t* = 0 to *t* = 6.0 ms.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
The variation of *V* with *t* can be described by

*V* = *A* sin *B**t*

where *A* and *B* are constants.

Determine the values of *A* and *B*. Give units with your answers.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.1
figures.alt: A coil in a uniform magnetic field is connected to a centre-zero voltmeter.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.2
figures.alt: A graph shows magnetic flux density varying periodically with time from 0 to 6 ms.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.3
figures.alt: A blank graph grid for induced e.m.f. V against time t, with axes marked from −V₀ to V₀ and 0 to 6 ms.
